title: What If Your Boss's Leadership Approach Is Less Effective Than Yours?
author: Kurt Mueller
summary: Kurt Mueller addresses leaders whose boss insists on a leadership approach, such as command-and-control, that conflicts with the collaborative, accountable style that already works for their team. He argues the answer depends less on whose style is better and more on understanding what results the boss wants. Using a financial services manager facing daily activity reports after costly errors, he shows that the boss is really worried about exposure and compliance. He offers four steps: identify the results your boss needs, translate the directive into your own approach, decide when to comply and when to push back, and propose a trial with agreed measures and a review date. Pushback should focus on evidence and results rather than a debate about styles. The closing thought is that the job is to demonstrate that your approach delivers what matters, not to prove you are the better leader.
points: Separate the outcome your boss wants from the method your boss prefers, since the disagreement is often about how rather than what.
Ask what concerns the boss most, what results would build confidence, and where you have flexibility.
Offer alternatives such as dashboards, exception reporting and weekly risk reviews that give oversight while preserving accountability.
Comply with legitimate policy and regulatory requirements, but respectfully push back when a method threatens team performance.
Propose a time-boxed trial with agreed measures and document what you learn to persuade a skeptical boss.
